01We followed the customer journey

What we found.
What we’d fix.

Six specific fixes across the website, social and local presence. Start here before sending more paid traffic.

Website & rewards

01Repair

Rewards takes
a wrong turn.

Toolkit’s FAQ link for viewing account information opens Terms and Conditions.

Our fix ↗

Correct the account/login route. Replace image-only tabs with labeled, keyboard-friendly controls.

02Simplify

Joining looks
like logging in.

The homepage rewards banner leads to a separate portal. The main site says new members must join in store.

Our fix ↗

Separate “Join in store” from “Member login,” with a nearby-yard button and a short explainer.

03Clarify

The entry fee
is a question.

Rancho’s location page requires admission but gives no fee amount. Part prices and core deposits sit elsewhere.

Our fix ↗

One local guide to fees, deposits, tools and returns. Pin a “Before You Pull” video.

Social & local

04Connect

The video links
are missing.

The homepage links to Facebook and X, but not Instagram, TikTok or YouTube.

Our fix ↗

Connect verified brand profiles. Run weekly Yard Finds across Reels, TikTok and Shorts with clear next steps.

05Align

Three different
store counts.

Homepage: 48. Seller page: 50. LinkedIn: 52, with Schnitzer Steel still in the company name.

Our fix ↗

One approved brand bio. Align the location count, ownership, descriptions and contact details across profiles.

06Correct

Local hours
don’t agree.

Rancho’s own page lists weekdays 9–6. Its Roadtrippers listing shows 8–5.

Our fix ↗

Confirm store and yard hours, correct directory listings, and maintain Google Business posts and review replies.

Keep the working inventory search and quote entry tools. Tighten the steps around them, then track the customer actions.
